campaign: MOSS in overgo does what the MOSS Ultra workflow does in ComfyUI, each section held to ComfyUI's recording

items.title: TestTheMOSSPassFusesWithoutChangingABit and its hand-recorded latents go: each fusion is held to its own chain bit for bit, and the latents were recorded from the code they checked

steps.title: TestTheMOSSPassFusesWithoutChangingABit and its hand-recorded latents go: each fusion is held to its own chain bit for bit, and the latents were recorded from the code they checked
steps.rationale:
The owner's review of 2026-11-22 (third), point 2, checked against the code and git: valid. fusionLatents were recorded five times (moss-checkpoint-regression, moss-merge-order, moss-situ-prologue, moss-attention-pass, fusion-edges-all/edges), each after a valid change of arithmetic broke them, and went stale at moss-encoder-own, which two slow runs found hours after it landed. The executor has no switch that compiles a pass unfused, so the test could not draw its reference in the run that checks it, and the last record, fusion-edges-all/edges', was the fused pass's own latent, justified by the chain test: from then the test held the code to itself. TestEachFusionMatchesItsChainWhereTheyCouldPart holds each of the 31 fusion kinds to its chain launched step by step, bit for bit, at four conditions, and TestEveryFusionKindHasAnEdgeCase refuses a kind without a case.

The change: the test, fusionLatents and the helpers only it reads go; the chain test is the check.

items.title: Every node by which the MOSS Ultra workflow saves, previews, compares or shows something has its counterpart in a run's result or on the page, and one without is refused without the card

steps.title: A depth section's comparison offers the picture its run started from, not the form's picture when the run completes
steps.rationale: SQA-463 (P2), checked against generation.js and workflow.js at 47b3587c9: valid; the review names this row its owner. When a depth section's run completes, the page reads the control picture from the form as it is then, not as the run was sent, so a picture changed while the run draws is labelled the run's source and offered in the A/B comparison beside the run's output, and the picture the run started from is not offered. The change: the page keeps the source each run was sent with and compares the run's outputs with that; a run followed after a reload offers a source only where its record names one, and the drawn and sharpened comparison stays. Check: TestWebUIBrowserMOSSComparesTheSourceItsRunStartedFrom sends a depth section with picture A, sets B in the form while it draws, and on completion the comparison offers A labelled as the source, beside the drawn and sharpened pictures.

items.title: A served MOSS picture is answered from its stored run only where every file it reads is present, its preset declared and its pair whole

steps.title: A MOSS request naming a file its answer reads that is absent is refused, naming it, before its stored answer is sought, and no answer is kept under an absent file
steps.rationale: SQA-406 (P2), checked against capabilityruntime.Contents at 47b3587c9: valid. A file a request's answer reads beside its model (a preset's adapter, the depth estimator) that is absent is written into the naming as "absent" and the request goes on, so a draw that finds the file installed by the time it opens it is kept under the absent key, and once the file is removed again the director answers the request from that run. The review's earlier points went with adapter-identity/do and beside-content/do; this one stayed. The change: Contents refuses a listed file that is absent, naming it, and Reading gives that refusal back instead of drawing afresh, which it still does for a naming it cannot make. Check: TestAnAbsentFileARequestReadsIsRefused names a request through Reading and Contents with one listed file absent: it is refused naming the file and the executor is never called; with the file present the request is served under the file's identity.

steps.title: A MOSS request naming a preset its model does not declare is refused as such at any size, before a picture it names is read
steps.rationale: SQA-425 (P2), checked at 47b3587c9: valid in its first part. Request.Sized reads the preset only when the request states no size, so with 1024 by 576 stated, admitted passes an undeclared preset, pictureFiles names nothing, Reading draws afresh, and onMiss reports the missing picture where the preset is at fault. Its second part, the enhancer's chat opened before a missing source is refused, went with enhanced-repeat/do: onMiss reads a request's pictures before it enhances. The change: admitted reads a named preset from the catalog at any size. Check: TestAnUndeclaredPresetIsRefusedAtAnySize sends an undeclared preset with no size and with 1024 by 576, a missing picture named in each, through preparedFirst with a stand-in session: each is refused naming the preset, and the session is never reached.

steps.title: A stored sharpened MOSS picture whose drawn picture was never kept is drawn again, so a run answers both pictures or draws them
steps.rationale: SQA-466 (P2), checked against keptDrawn at 47b3587c9: valid. keptDrawn publishes the drawn PNG and its derived-from edge after the run has kept the sharpened one, so a process stopped between the two leaves a stored answer with no drawn parent, and every repeat finds it and returns the sharpened picture alone, as a success. The change: a replayed sharpened picture whose drawn one the store does not hold is no answer, and the request is drawn afresh and both kept. Check: TestAStoredSharpenedPictureWithoutItsDrawnOneIsDrawnAgain keeps a sharpened answer with no drawn parent through the served-repeat stand-in: its repeat draws again and returns both pictures, and a whole pair is replayed with no draw.

steps.title: A MOSS request reads its selected profile once, where its preset, canvas or adapters ask for it, and a plain repeat reads none
steps.rationale: SQA-461 (P2), checked against pictureFiles and preparedFirst in image_cuda_windows.go at 47b3587c9: valid on the served path. Reading names a picture request's files through pictureFiles, which reads and parses the selected profile (pictureCatalog), and preparedFirst reads it again to size the request, so every request reads its profile twice before the director seeks its stored answer, and a plain repeat, which names no preset, canvas or adapter, needs neither read. The review's other part, Generator.Reset and prepare each opening model_index.json again on a changed seed, is in the generator, which the served-repeat check stands in for; it goes with served-parts, whose ledger reads that part's time. The change: a request's catalog is read once, where its preset, canvas or adapters ask for it, and passed on to the sizing. Check: TestARepeatedPictureReadsNoProfile serves a plain picture twice and one naming a preset through the served-repeat stand-in, counting the profile's reads: none for the plain repeat, one for the preset request.

items.title: One rule says when a file's identity may be taken without reading it: a size-and-time memo is a claim its next read proves byte for byte, and the video encoder's 11 GB checkpoint is proven so

steps.title: One rule says when a file's identity may be taken without reading it: a size-and-time memo is a claim its next read proves byte for byte, and the video encoder's 11 GB checkpoint is proven so
steps.rationale:
The owner's review of 2026-11-22 (second), point 2, checked against the code: valid. adapter-hold names a file beside a model by its bytes, read once a process through the handle that holds it (heldfile.Set.Identity), and declined to name it by size and modification time: integrity before speed. discovery.Memo names a file by size and modification time across processes (memo.go lookup), and its Claim says whoever reads the bytes next must prove the claim, a claim they do not carry failing that read. The video text encoder's checkpoint is admitted so: latentvideo admitCheckpoint passes discovery.FileIdentity over a memo to pytorchzip.Admit, which returns the remembered identity without reading the file when known() answers, and the encoder then reads its tensors by offset; nothing proves the 11 GB, so a checkpoint replaced under the same size and time would be named as the one it replaced. The two rules disagree, and the memo's own is not kept.

The rule the row states, at heldfile and discovery.Memo alike: a file's identity is its bytes. A memo of size and time may name it before it is read only as a claim, and the read that next takes every byte (the encoder's load) hashes them as it reads and fails where they are not the claim's; a file no read takes whole is hashed once a process through its held handle. The video encoder's admission carries the claim to its load, which proves it.

Check: TestAClaimedCheckpointIsProvenByItsRead, card-free on a small checkpoint: a claim whose file was replaced under its size and time fails the load that reads it; a true claim loads with no second read.

items.title: Video names the files it reads beside its model as pictures do, once a process through the held files, so a replaced file is refused while in use

steps.title: Video names the files it reads beside its model as pictures do, once a process through the held files, so a replaced file is refused while in use
steps.rationale:
The owner's review of 2026-11-22 (second), point 1, checked against the code: valid. Pictures name what they read beside their model one way (heldfile.Set: hashed once through a handle held while a session or request owns it, so it cannot be replaced while in use). Video names its four another way each: the text encoder checkpoint by a size-and-time memo and an archive map (promptEncoders.archives, file-identity-rule); the finish runtime's libraries, 792 MB, hashed once a process and not held (finish_windows.go runtimeIdentity); the tokenizer's two files hashed on every request (prompt_encoder.go, TextConditioningSpec.content); FFmpeg hashed for every clip (mp4.go, NewMP4Encoder).

The change: each goes through heldfile.Set as pictures' adapters do, owned by the video session or the request, so each is read once a process and held while in use, and the three other mechanisms are removed. A rule refuses a new one: artifact.IdentifyFile on a file a served path reads beside its model is reached only through heldfile.Set (internal/repoanalysis), so a capability added later names its files the same way.

Check: TestAServedClipReusesItsHeldFiles, card-free with a stand-in session as TestAServedPictureReusesItsHeldFiles: the tokenizer and FFmpeg opened and hashed once across two clips, none written or renamed onto while held, and let go after.

items.title: Every served path's request is split into its parts, each with its wall, processor time and bytes read, as the MOSS workflow's clock reads them, so time outside the model shows on each

steps.title: Every served path's request is split into its parts, each with its wall, processor time and bytes read, as the MOSS workflow's clock reads them, so time outside the model shows on each
steps.rationale:
The owner's review of 2026-11-22 (second), point 3, checked against the code: partly valid. The parts ledger exists for every served path (processmeasure.Stages): the session director marks the request read, the stored answer sought, the named inputs read, the session leased and the run recorded, the workflow runtime marks each stage by its module, video marks its own (prompt rows, denoising, decoding, the clip written) and chat its load's (cmd/recipe inference_measure). But a part records its wall and the device's peak alone, speech marks none of its own, and only the MOSS workflow's clock reads a request's parts beside each one's processor time and bytes read (latentimage TestTheUltraWorkflowIsTimedInItsOrder, readProcessUse, written into that test), which is how adapter-hold's per-request hashing was found.

The change: a part records its processor time and the bytes the process read inside it (processmeasure.Part), so every ledger carries what the MOSS clock computed by hand; speech marks its parts as video does; and the recipe command's measure reports every served task's parts, not chat's load alone. The MOSS clock reads the ledger in place of its own counters.

Check: TestEachServedPathSplitsItsRequestIntoParts serves a picture, a clip, speech and a chat turn through their capabilities with stand-in sessions under a ledger: each request's parts name its load or lease, its stages and its recording, each with wall, processor time and bytes read, their walls inside the request's.

Note: SQA-468 (P3) and the generator part of SQA-461 go with this step, as the parts they cost show in its ledger: the finished PNG is rebuilt with its texts by the workflow's output encoder, keptDrawn and the workspace's OutputContent though the generator wrote them once (three full rewrites a fresh draw, two a repeat, withPictureTexts allocating a whole buffer even where every chunk matches), and Generator.Reset and prepare each open model_index.json again on a changed seed. Where the ledger shows them, PNGContent keeps bytes already carrying the texts it would write, the artifact ID unchanged, and the catalog is read once a session.

items.title: The MOSS golden floors are read before a section is drawn and refuse a reference of no signal, and the sharpened pair's check compares pixels

steps.title: The sharpened pair's check compares the pictures' pixels, so a finishing that changes none is refused
steps.rationale: SQA-467 (P2: a check that passes without checking), checked against sharpened_pair_windows_test.go at 47b3587c9: valid. The test strips the pictures' texts before it holds the drawn picture equal to the plain one, but holds the finished picture apart from the unsharpened one by their PNG bytes, and only the finished PNG carries Finishing=sharpened, so a finishing that returned its input's pixels would pass. The change: the inequality compares decoded pixels, the drawn-equals-plain comparison as it is. Check: the test itself, which a finishing that changes no pixel now fails.

steps.title: The MOSS golden floors are declared before a section is drawn, each failed comparison is reported and its generator closed, and a reference of no signal is refused
steps.rationale: SQA-410 (P2), checked against golden_floor_windows_model_test.go and decibelsOverSquares at 47b3587c9: valid. holdGoldenFloors draws every case (readGoldenCases) before it asks whether each declares a floor, so a missing declaration costs five baseline draws and five controls; a later case's size error stops the test before an earlier failure is reported or the open generator closed; each control encodes a PNG it throws away; and a reference of all zeros scores -Inf in both precision modes, which holdMergedSections accepts as equal. The change: floors are checked before any draw, a comparison's failure is reported as it is scored and its generator closed by Cleanup, a control keeps its latent alone, and decibelsOverSquares refuses a reference with no signal while agreement with a nonzero one stays +Inf. Check: the floors test itself, with card-free cases for the refusals where they need no draw.

items.title: A MOSS sampling refines its prompt once a request and makes its control's zeros once, its pictures bit for bit as before

steps.title: A MOSS sampling makes its control's zeros on their first use alone
steps.rationale: SQA-430 (P2), checked against controlAt in rotary_sampling_windows.go at 47b3587c9: valid. controlAt allocates the control's zeros on the host before it asks whether the card already holds them, so the 28 steps of the depth section's pass-2 recording outside the control window allocate 56 buffers for one upload, 123.75 MiB of host allocation a draw. The change: the slot is chosen first and the zeros made only for its first upload. Check: TestASamplingMakesItsControlZerosOnce runs the control selection over a schedule with steps inside and outside the window and counts one zero buffer made.

steps.title: MOSS refines a request's prompt once a branch, not at every pass, its latent bit for bit the per-pass program's
steps.rationale: SQA-422 (P2), checked against compileRotaryDenoiserProgram at 47b3587c9: valid. textGraph.refine reads the branch's prompt and the text's rotary rows alone, no timestep and no latent, yet sits in the per-pass graph, so a 50-step guided request refines each of its two prompts 50 times. The saving is unmeasured; the workflow's clock (TestTheUltraWorkflowIsTimedInItsOrder) reads it after the change. The change: the refinement runs once a branch a request and the pass reads its rows from the card. Check: TestThePromptIsRefinedOnceARequest draws a few steps of text-to-image, counts one refinement a branch, and holds the latent bit for bit to the program that refines in its pass, which the test builds from the same graph.

items.title: The workflow clock refuses a record it cannot write before it draws, and a ComfyUI recording binds each output to what made it

steps.title: The workflow clock refuses a record path that is not relative to the repository before it holds the machine or draws a section
steps.rationale: SQA-460 (P2), checked against readWorkflowSource and appendWorkflowTiming at 47b3587c9: valid. An absolute OVERGO_WORKFLOW_RECORD is accepted at the start and joined under the repository only when the timing is appended, after both runs, so the attempt reported in d28ab1e84 drew twelve sections (81 s measured) and saved nothing. The change: the record path is checked, relative and inside the repository, before the quiet machine is asked for. Check: TestTheWorkflowClockRefusesARecordItCannotWrite gives the source check an absolute path and one leaving the repository: each is refused before any draw.

steps.title: A ComfyUI recording binds a resumed output to the prompt that made it, keeps two files of one name apart, and credits a repeat only from two prompts
steps.rationale: SQA-388 (P2), checked against cmd/comfy-reference/record.go at 47b3587c9: valid. record resumes a prompt on its request hash and prompt ID alone after reading the current models and commits; await starts sampling memory at a retry; keep names a file by its node and base name, so two files of one name from one node in different subfolders overwrite each other; and the paired-recording check asks each run for a prompt ID but never compares them, so one capture given twice passes as two runs. The three pairs at 89cf0f0e3 have distinct prompt IDs. The change: a resumed output keeps the producer it was recorded under and is refused when the models or commits moved; memory sampling begun on a retry says so; a kept file's name holds its subfolder; and a pair's prompt IDs differ. Check: TestARecordingBindsEachOutputToWhatMadeIt drives record against a stand-in ComfyUI for each case.

items.title: SenseNova's request-resources test is measured again on a card to itself and carries modeltest, so the gate's cuda lane runs no real-model test

steps.title: SenseNova's request-resources test is measured again on a card to itself and carries modeltest, so the gate's cuda lane runs no real-model test
steps.rationale:
The evidence: cuda-synthetic/tag moved every untagged CUDA test that reads the data root behind modeltest but one. TestSenseNovaVariableRequestResources runs SenseNova's 8B production generation in an isolated measurement process, and docs/image_video_capacity.json names its retained measurement by the bytes of its file (evidence:sha256:888854b5...), which the store holds; tagged, its bytes changed and TestImageVideoCapacityAcceptance found no evidence under the new identity. A measurement is taken again only on a card to itself, and the readings campaign holds the card until its Wan arms are drawn, so the file stays in the gate, named by the check as measuredInPlace, and this row follows the campaign.

The change: the test carries //go:build modeltest, it is measured again on a quiet card into the store, the capacity record and its protocol digest (imageVideoCapacitySHA256) name the new identity, and measuredInPlace goes, so internal/sensenovarecipe leaves the cuda lane.

Check: a whole-tree test with measuredInPlace gone, named afresh so it fails before the change: TestTheGateRunsNoRealModelTest.

Refiled 2026-11-16 from cuda-resources/do, whose step carried no card need, so dispatch gave it while the readings campaign held the card: this step carries -needs-card and waits for a card to itself.

decisions.question: skill.md's 227 rule lines each cite a check. Read at 3ba4de8c7: the first check of 181 has a doc comment and of 45 has none, and the comments state what their test holds, not the rule that cites it ("purpose = recursive self-improvement ..." cites TestCycleFilesDeclinesAndAcceptsNothing, whose comment is the cycle's comparisons; "scorecard columns = ..." cites TestScorecardRowsEveryServableModel, whose comment is rows and dashes). Writing skill.md from the comments as they stand changes what it says. Which form does skill.md take?
options: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
skill.md holds its terms and judgement lines alone; the rule lines go, each check saying its rule when it refuses
skill.md is written from the tests' doc comments as they stand, its wording changing to theirs
decisions.recommendation: Each rule line moves onto its first check as a doc-comment line of its own, and skill.md is generated from those lines and its judgement section, so it says what it says now, each rule written once on its check
